function.name: requests_get
function.description: Sends a GET request to the specified URL to retrieve weather data from the Open-Meteo API. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: URL of the Open-Meteo API endpoint.

headers.description: Headers to include in the request. Each key-value pair represents a header field and its value.

Content-Type.description: The MIME type of the body of the request (used with POST and PUT requests).

Accept.description: Media type(s) that is/are acceptable for the response.

timeout.description: Maximum time in seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up. This is a float type value.

params.description: Query parameters for the GET request.

latitude.description: Latitude of the location, positive for N and negative for S. This is a float type value.

longitude.description: Longitude of the location, positive for E and negative for W. This is a float type value.

elevation.description: Elevation in meters above sea level for the location. The default value represents no elevation downscaling.

auth.description: Authentication tuple for HTTP authentication, in the format (username, password).

cert.description: Path to the SSL client certificate file (.pem). A null value means no client certificate is used.

cookies.description: Dictionary of cookies to send with the request. Each key represents a cookie name.

proxies.description: Dictionary mapping protocol names to the URL of the proxy. Each key-value pair represents a protocol and its proxy URL.

stream.description: If True, the response should be streamed; otherwise, it should be downloaded immediately.

verify.description: Whether to verify the server's TLS certificate.

Here’s a quick snapshot of the **next big festivals happening in the United States** (sorted by the earliest upcoming date). All dates are for the 2026 calendar year unless otherwise noted.  

| Festival | Dates | Location | What to Expect | Why It’s Worth Checking Out |
|----------|-------|----------|----------------|-----------------------------|
| **Coachella Valley Music & Arts Festival** | **April 14–18, 2026** | Indio, California (Empire Polo Club) | 5‑day music extravaganza featuring top‑tier rock, pop, hip‑hop, indie, and electronic acts, plus art installations, food trucks, and a “Coachella‑style” fashion scene. | The world’s most iconic music festival; huge line‑ups, immersive art, and a chance to see artists you’ve been waiting for. |
| **Austin City Limits (ACL) Music Festival** | **May 12–15, 2026** | Austin, Texas (Zilker Park) | 4‑day festival with a mix of mainstream and indie acts across multiple stages, plus food, art, and a “Music & Food” partnership. | One of the largest free‑entry festivals in the U.S., ACL offers a blend of local culture and international stars. |
| **New Orleans Jazz & Heritage Festival** | **May 27–28, 2026** | New Orleans, Louisiana (Frenchmen Street & French Market) | 2‑day celebration of jazz, blues, funk, and world music, with live cooking demos, street vendors, and cultural exhibits. | A deep dive into New Orleans’ musical heritage and culinary traditions. |
| **Lollapalooza Chicago** | **August 4–7, 2026** | Chicago, Illinois (Grant Park) | 4‑day festival featuring a wide range of genres, from rock to hip‑hop to electronic, plus art installations and food trucks. | The largest music festival in the Midwest, known for its diverse line‑up and vibrant atmosphere. |
| **Bonnaroo Music & Arts Festival** | **June 29–July 2, 2026** | Manchester, Tennessee (Bonnaroo Music & Arts Festival Grounds) | 4‑day festival with a mix of indie, hip‑hop, country, and world music, plus art, yoga, and a “Bonnaroo” community vibe. | Known for its eclectic line‑up and “Bonnaroo” community spirit. |
| **Summerfest** | **July 20–25, 2026** | Milwaukee, Wisconsin (American Family Field) | 6‑day festival featuring a mix of mainstream and indie acts, plus food, craft beer, and a “Summerfest” vibe. | The world’s largest music festival, with a focus on family‑friendly entertainment. |
| **Burning Man** | **August 22–30, 2026** | Black Rock Desert, Nevada | 9‑day event focused on art, self‑expression, and community, with a temporary city built entirely by participants. | A unique cultural experience that blends art, music, and community. |

---

### How to Make the Most of Your Festival Experience

| Tip | Why It Helps |
|-----|--------------|
| **Buy tickets early** | Many festivals sell out months in advance. |
| **Plan your travel & lodging** | Popular festivals attract crowds; book flights and hotels early. |
| **Check the line‑up** | Line‑ups change frequently; confirm your favorite artists. |
| **Pack essentials** | Sunscreen, water bottle, portable charger, and a small backpack. |
| **Stay hydrated & eat well** | Festivals can be long; keep energy levels up. |
| **Explore local culture** | Many festivals incorporate local food, art, and traditions. |

---

### Need More Specific Info?

If you’re looking for a particular type of festival (e.g., food, film, tech, or niche music), let me know and I can narrow down the list or add more details such as ticket prices, transportation options, or recommended accommodations.
